newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Power restored to parts of Kabul after long break.
newsitem.headline: Power restored to parts of Kabul after long break.

text.p: Electricity has been restored to parts of the Afghan capital Kabul for the first time since being cut in fighting following an abortive coup in January 1994, government officials said on Tuesday.

Power came on in the city centre, the northern suburb of Khair Khana and the diplomatic enclave of Wazir Akbar Khan on Monday after transmission lines were connected to Sarobi, 60 km (37 miles) east of Kabul.
But almost 65 percent of Kabul's population remained without electricity because of badly damaged power lines.
Supplies were cut to Kabul after an attempted coup by Prime Minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar and opposition warlord General Abdul Rashid Dostum in January 1994 which led to fighting.
Hekmatyar rejoined the government as prime minister last June after a peace pact with President Burhanuddin Rabbani.
